business.description: Primo Chemicals Limited is a chlor-alkali manufacturer delivering essential chemical solutions to a wide range of industries. The company operates a backward-integrated business model with a manufacturing facility at Naya Nangal, Punjab, combining integrated operations with a diversified product portfolio.

outlook.statement: FY27 is designated as the year of execution where balance sheet investments begin converting into operating cash flows. Three engines of margin expansion converging: Flow Tech acquisition completion, 50 MW captive solar plant commissioning, and downstream product portfolio scale-up.
The convergence of these engines within a single financial year is designed to lift the company's margin floor permanently.

India's chemical industry is at a structural inflection point with domestic manufacturing expanding, supply chains re-routing toward reliable producing nations, and downstream applications growing at rates outpacing the economy.

India's chlor-alkali industry at edge of structural upcycle driven by domestic manufacturing expansion, infrastructure investment, water treatment mandates, and pharmaceutical growth; global supply chain diversification (China-plus-one) creating selective openings for Indian chemical producers; water treatment and sanitation focus creating sustained demand for chlorine-based products.

Q1 FY2026-27 showed improved profitability with combined average sales realization of Rs 46,598 per ECU (up Rs 5,477 YoY), net profit before tax of Rs 8.86 crore on sales turnover of Rs 140.27 crore, despite capacity utilization decreasing to 73% from 83% YoY.

Global economic outlook expected to remain shaped by moderate growth, inflation volatility, geopolitical uncertainty and changing trade flows. Demand from manufacturing, infrastructure and consumer-facing sectors expected to support industrial activity.

India's economy expected to remain supported by domestic demand, manufacturing activity, infrastructure investments and policy-led industrial development, supporting demand across end-use sectors relevant to Primo Chemicals.

Indian chemical industry expected to grow at 8-9% annually over next five to six years, potentially reaching USD 230-255 billion. Continued manufacturing expansion, infrastructure investments, specialty chemical demand and global supply-chain diversification expected to support growth.

Indian chlor-alkali market reached approximately USD 2.5 billion in 2025 and projected to grow to USD 3.6 billion by 2034 at CAGR of around 4.0%. Indian caustic soda market expected to expand steadily long-term.

Primo Chemicals is well positioned to benefit from medium-term opportunities across the chlor-alkali value chain. Rising demand for caustic soda and chlorine derivatives from aluminium, pulp and paper, textiles, pharmaceuticals, infrastructure, water treatment and industrial manufacturing is expected to support long-term consumption growth.

Global supply-chain diversification and the China-plus-one approach may create selective opportunities for Indian chemical manufacturers. Primo's regional presence in Northern India, integrated operations and diversified product portfolio position it to explore these opportunities in a measured manner.

As the industry prioritises energy efficiency, sustainability and integration, Primo Chemicals' focus on captive power, renewable energy, downstream integration and operational efficiency positions it favourably to create sustainable long-term value.

The Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) project is currently under implementation as a Work-in-Progress (WIP) project under the Company's water management initiatives. It will facilitate effective treatment of wastewater/effluent, reduce environmental impact, support improved water quality, promote wastewater recycling and reuse, reduce freshwater consumption, and contribute to sustainable water resource management.
Planning to conduct Life Cycle Assessments (LCA) in a phased manner in future.
Under Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) for FY 2025-26 to FY 2026-27 with notified targets for GHG emission intensity.
Preparing a business continuity document outlining probable risks (social, financial, environmental, strategic) and mitigation measures to ensure uninterrupted business continuity.
The Company expects to generate positive cashflows from its operations in the foreseeable future and will be able to meet its obligations for at least 12 months from the balance sheet date.
